Diagnosis:
CAUSE: Certificate `shop-tls` in namespace `shop` expires in about an hour because its `spec.duration` is `1h`, so it is a deliberately short-lived lab certificate, not a failed renewal.

EVIDENCE:
- `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get -n shop certificate shop-tls -o jsonpath=...` (my check): `spec.duration=1h`, `spec.renewBefore=10m`, `status.notAfter=2026-11-01T01:06:42Z`, `status.renewalTime=2026-11-01T00:56:42Z`.
- diag-k8s, `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get -n shop certificates -o yaml`: `spec.issuerRef` is `Issuer/lab-selfsigned`, `status.revision: 1`.
- diag-k8s, `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab describe -n shop certificate shop-tls`: condition `Ready=True`, reason `Ready`, message "Certificate is up to date and has not expired".
- diag-k8s, `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get -n shop certificaterequests,issuers`: `shop-tls-1` APPROVED=True, READY=True; `lab-selfsigned` READY=True.
- diag-k8s, `kubectl --context kind-sre-lab get -n shop events`: a Warning `BadConfig` says the certificate "will be issued with an empty Issuer DN". This is a separate issue from expiry, and I did not verify it.

FIX (not applied): raise `spec.duration` on `shop/shop-tls` from `1h` to a normal lifetime (for example `2160h`), or, if the 1h lifetime is intentional for the lab, change the `LabCertificateExpiringSoon` threshold so it does not fire on this certificate.

Fact.Name: expiry
Fact.Value: `notAfter` about one hour after it was issued: expires in under 60 minutes

Fact.Name: cause
Fact.Value: `duration: 1h` on the Certificate (with `renewBefore: 10m`), issued by Issuer `lab-selfsigned`

Fact.Name: fix (not applied)
Fact.Value: set a real duration (for example `2160h`) and renew; or force a renewal now
